digest.component_or_area: BindingStore core subsystem (binding_store.py, binding_repository.py, binding_lifecycle.py, binding_recovery.py)
propositions: BindingStore's 799-line monolithic module conflates byte persistence, lifecycle policy, and recovery logic with no cohesive owner for new safety rules and mutation guards.

Decompose behind a unified public facade into three internal owners (repository, lifecycle, recovery) while preserving all stored formats, signatures, unknown fields, JSON serialization, and shallow all_bindings() compatibility.

Implement journal-free retirement completion: durable tombstone is authoritative intent; live forward/reverse pairs are removed only when all three identities (tombstone, forward, reverse) agree; only explicit unretire revokes intent.

Live recovery must run after staleness validation but before remote issue observation to prevent interleaving new liveness evidence with completion; create and keyed recovery must be idempotent and abort on identity mismatch or ambiguity.
Automatic liveness signals (404 grace, same-key confirm, absent count) cannot resurrect a tombstoned identity; only explicit unretire removes the tombstone and eliminates the completion candidate.

Each decomposition slice is independently revertible with unchanged stored formats and public signatures; slices preserve rotation order, selective five-file publication, pending/confirmed/retired rules, and immutable comment identity.
